newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices gain on buying by state firms.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices gain on buying by state firms.

text.p: Indian cotton prices recovered on Friday after recent losses, as state firms stepped up purchases, dealers said.
Arrivals also remained limited at producing centres as farmers were bringing fewer quantities due to lower prices.
Dealers said among spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 10/15 rupees to 815/845 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned rose by 10 rupees at 1,375/1,625 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) rose by 100 rupees to 18,000/18,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) for the superior type while the average one was steady at 16,500/17,500 rupees.
